title: Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs
subtitle: Sticky-sweet chicken thighs in a garlicky honey glaze, piled over steaming rice.

items.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar
cornstarch + 1 tbsp cold water (optional, for a thicker glaze) — cornstarch qty scales, water is per batch of slurry

steps: Sear the chicken. Pat dry, season with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high, add chicken in a single layer, cook 5-6 minutes turning once, until golden and 165F inside. Work in batches if crowded.
Wake up the aromatics. Reduce to medium, stir in garlic and ginger, cook about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Build the glaze. Add honey, soy sauce, and vinegar. Simmer 1-2 minutes, scraping up browned bits.
Thicken, if you like. Stir in cornstarch slurry, simmer 1-2 minutes until glossy and clinging. Skip for a lighter sauce.
Finish. Taste and adjust — more honey for sweetness, vinegar for brightness. Toss to coat.
Serve. Spoon over rice, top with scallions and sesame seeds.

title: Bulgogi-Style Ground Beef Bowls
subtitle: Crispy-edged ground beef in a sweet-spicy gochujang glaze, over rice with scallions.

items.name: neutral oil (only needed with lean beef)
Optional: julienned carrots, sliced cucumber, kimchi, a fried egg

steps: Start the rice first — about 12-15 minutes hands-free.
Brown the beef. Large skillet over medium-high, 4-5 minutes breaking into crumbles; leave undisturbed a minute between stirs for crispy edges. Drain excess fat if needed.
Add aromatics. Stir in garlic and ginger, about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Glaze it. Add soy sauce, gochujang, brown sugar. Cook 2 minutes until sauce coats and glazes the beef.
Off the heat, finish. Stir in sesame oil last (it burns off if added too early).
Build the bowls. Spoon beef over rice, top with scallions and sesame seeds, plus any extra toppings.

title: Steak & Cheese Hoagies
subtitle: Shaved ribeye with sweet peppers, onion, and melty provolone in toasted hoagie rolls.

items.name: ribeye, very thinly sliced against the grain
salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Toast the rolls. Split and broil 2-3 minutes until golden at edges — watch closely.
Cook the vegetables. Half the oil, medium-high, pepper and onion 5-6 minutes until softened with charred edges. Set aside.
Sear the steak. Season with salt, pepper, garlic powder. Remaining oil over high heat, single layer 60-90 seconds per side, in batches if needed.
Melt the cheese. Stir vegetables back in, lay provolone over top, cover 1-2 minutes until melty.
Assemble. Pile steak, vegetables, and cheese into toasted rolls, serve immediately.
notes: Tip: chill ribeye 20-30 minutes in freezer first — firm meat slices much thinner.

title: Honey Sriracha Glazed Chicken with Rice
subtitle: Sweet-heat chicken in a sticky honey-sriracha glaze, over jasmine rice with broccoli.

items.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs or tenders, cut into bite-size pieces
1½ tbsp sriracha (more or less to taste)
rice vinegar or a squeeze of lime (optional)

steps: Start the rice first. Cook jasmine rice per package, about 15 minutes.
Mix the glaze. Whisk honey, sriracha, soy sauce, and garlic in a small bowl.

Sear the chicken. Pat dry, season with salt, pepper, garlic powder. Oil in large skillet over medium-high, single layer, sear undisturbed 3-4 minutes, stir and cook 3-4 minutes more, browned and 165F.
Steam the broccoli. Microwave per bag, about 4 minutes, while chicken finishes.
Glaze it. Reduce to medium, pour glaze over chicken, toss 1-2 minutes until thickened and sticky. Stir in vinegar/lime if using.
Serve. Chicken over rice, broccoli alongside, sesame seeds and scallions if you like.

title: Crunchy Garlic Sesame Chicken
subtitle: Crispy cornstarch-coated chicken thighs tossed in a honey sesame sauce, from Easy Meals for 2, Ep 34

items.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
green onions (whites for the sauce and greens to garnish)
cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water, to thicken the sauce if needed

steps: Prepare the chicken: mix chicken with seasonings and oil (oil helps seasonings spread better), then add cornstarch and mix.
Mix the sauce: in a bowl, combine the soy sauce, honey, brown sugar, rice vinegar, ketchup, sesame oil and water. Keep the cornstarch slurry separate.

Fry: heat about 1/2 inch of neutral oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken in batches for 5-7 minutes total, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked through to 74°C / 165°F. Transfer to a wire rack.

Cook the sauce: carefully discard the frying oil, leaving about 1 tsp in the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add the garlic and ginger; stir for 20-30 seconds. Pour in the sauce and bring to a gentle simmer.
Thicken: stir the slurry again, then add it to the sauce. Simmer for 30-60 seconds until glossy and thick enough to coat the chicken.
Toss and serve: add the chicken and sesame seeds. Toss briefly until coated, then serve immediately over rice with green onions.
notes: Source: Facebook save

title: Honey Garlic Chicken (Zachs.foods)
subtitle: Cornstarch-coated chicken thighs in a honey garlic sauce, from Recipes That Are Better Than Takeout Ep 45
steps: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, a little oil and cornstarch, and mix until coated.
For the sauce, combine soy sauce, honey, red pepper flakes, paprika, water, garlic and sugar. Whisk together.
Heat oil, add the chicken and cook until 165°F and golden brown.
In the same pan, add the green onion whites, then add the sauce mixture and let it thicken.
Toss the chicken in the sauce and serve.
notes: Source: Facebook save, Zachs.foods. Caption says full recipe is in bio; steps condensed from video transcript, which is truncated, and transcript also mentions butter melting in the pan though butter is not in the caption ingredient list.

title: 4-Ingredient No Knead Bread
subtitle: Same-day no-knead loaf made with 00 flour, yeast, salt and hot water

items.name: hot water (use 1.75 cups for a wetter dough and better product, per source)

steps: Put 3 1/4 cups flour in a bowl (sift if you want). Add 2 tsp yeast and about 1 tsp salt.
Add 1 1/2 cups hot water (or 1 3/4 cups for a wetter dough). Mix, using a wet hand if needed, and scrape down the sides. It should look shaggy.
Cover with a towel and let rise for 2 hours, until doubled in size.
After the bread has been rising for 1 hour, set the oven to 450°F and put 2 inches of water in an oven-safe bowl on the bottom rack of the oven.
Flour your surface, turn the dough out, and flour the top. Do not knead. Fold it onto itself, then cut an X on top with a sharp knife.
Flour a pizza stone (or use a Dutch oven lined with parchment) and place the dough on it. Bake for 35 minutes.
Slice or tear and serve.
notes: Source: Facebook save, Therecessionchef. Caption calls it a 30-minute bread, but the transcript describes about 5 minutes of mixing, a 2-hour rise and a 35-minute bake.

title: Crockpot Mongolian Beef & Noodles
subtitle: Seared chuck roast slow-cooked in a sweet and savory Mongolian-style sauce with lo mein noodles

items.name: SPG or favorite seasoning, for the beef
chili crisp oil, optional, if you want heat

steps: Season the beef with SPG or your favorite seasoning. Heat a skillet over high heat with the butter and sear the beef in small batches for 1-2 minutes per side, building color without cooking it through.
Transfer the beef to the crockpot. Deglaze the skillet with a splash of the measured beef broth, scrape up the browned bits, and pour everything into the crockpot.
Add the remaining broth, shoyu, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, rice vinegar and black pepper. Stir gently.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4 to 5 hours or HIGH for 2.5 to 3.5 hours, checking early so the thin beef stays tender without falling apart.
Mix the cornstarch with the cold water to make a slurry. Stir the slurry into the sauce and cook on HIGH for 15-20 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Slice the green onions into 1-inch pieces. Separate the precooked noodles and add them directly to the crockpot. Toss everything together and heat on HIGH for 5-10 minutes.
Finish with sliced green onions, sesame seeds, and chili crisp oil if you want heat, then serve immediately. Do not leave the noodles sitting on KEEP WARM - they will keep drinking up the sauce.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Step 5 in the source also says to mix the slurry 'with a cup of broth'; the listed slurry ingredients are cornstarch and cold water.

title: Beef with Broccoli (Zachs.foods)
subtitle: Takeout-style beef and broccoli stir fry, from Recipes That Are Better Than Takeout Ep 33
steps: Slice the beef against the grain and add it to a bowl with baking soda, soy sauce, cornstarch, oyster sauce, pepper and water. Let it marinate while you make the sauce.
Make the sauce with soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, cornstarch and water, and whisk together.
Sear the beef in a hot pan with oil, about 1 minute per side, then saute the ginger and garlic.
Add the broccoli, beef and sauce to the pan and cook together.
Serve with rice, with sesame seeds sprinkled on top.
notes: Source: Facebook save, Zachs.foods. Caption says full recipe is in bio; transcript names the ingredients but gives no quantities, so all quantities are unknown.

title: Beijing Beef
subtitle: Crispy fried steak tossed with bell pepper, onion and a sweet-tangy sauce - serves 3-4

items.name: skirt steak or flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
small red bell pepper, large diced
water (add an extra 0.5 tbsp if needed)

steps: In a bowl, combine sesame oil, garlic powder, baking soda, kosher salt and white pepper with the flank steak. Mix well, then add cornstarch and water and mix until the meat is craggly. Set aside.
In a small bowl, combine vinegar, oyster sauce, ketchup, hoisin sauce, soy sauce, sugar and chili flakes. Mix well and set aside.

In a large pan, heat enough oil for a shallow fry to 350°F. Carefully place the marinated beef in the oil, ensuring slices do not stick together. Fry for 3-4 minutes or until cooked through, coated and crispy. Strain the beef and set aside.
In a large wok, heat 1-2 tbsp oil. Add onions and bell peppers and saute for 30 seconds or just before they turn translucent. Add garlic and ginger and saute another 30 seconds to 1 minute.

Make a pit in the center and pour in all of the sauce. Toss with the onions and bell peppers, then add the fried beef. Toss until everything is combined and evenly coated with the sauce. Serve and enjoy.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Source states serves 3-4.

title: Papa Tea's Chinese BBQ Pork
subtitle: Marinated pork butt steaks air-fried or oven-baked until deeply golden - serves 5-6

items.name: pork butt or pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2 inch steak pieces

steps: In a bowl combine sugar, oyster sauce, shaoxing wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, chicken bouillon, five spice, onion powder, garlic powder and salt (add food dye here, optional). Mix well.
Slice pork into 1 1/2 inch steaks, then marinate with the sauce mixture for 1 hour or overnight for best results in the fridge.
Air fryer: set air fryer to 350°F and air fry for 35-40 minutes. Flip pork over every 10 minutes to ensure it does not burn.

Oven: set oven to 350°F. Fill an oven-safe container with hot water and leave on a second rack under the top rack. Bake marinated pork on a baking sheet for 45 minutes to 1 hour, flipping every 15 minutes.
Cook until pork is 145°F and the edges are deeply golden. Rest for 15-20 minutes before serving. Chop into bite-sized pieces and enjoy.
notes: Source: Facebook save, Stephvnietea. Source states serves 5-6.

title: Homemade Hamburger Helper
subtitle: One-pan ground beef and elbow noodles in tomato soup and broth, topped with cheddar - 12 large servings for meal prep
steps: In a pan, cook down the beef and onions with the seasoning.
Add in garlic and tomato soup.
Add in the Brami noodles.
Add in beef bone broth and chicken bouillon.
Stir, cover and let simmer until the noodles are done and the liquid is absorbed.
Top with cheese and enjoy.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Source gives 430 cals, 44g protein, 22g carb, 17g fat and states 12 large servings.

title: Papa Tea's Mongolian Beef
subtitle: Restaurant-style flank steak wok-fried with onions and green onions in a savory sauce, served with rice

items.name: flank steak, sliced against the grain
green onions, cut into large chunks
oil, generous amount for shallow frying
white pepper (transcript wording unclear; black pepper noted as alternative)

steps: Cut the green onions into large chunks. Mince the garlic, chop the onions, and peel the ginger with a spoon and grate it.

Slice the flank steak against the grain into big pieces. Tenderize with baking soda, then add cornstarch, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, cooking wine and white pepper. Mix well and marinate for 15 minutes.
Make the sauce with oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, soy sauce, sugar, chicken bouillon, white pepper and a little sesame oil.
Heat a generous amount of oil in a wok until nice and hot and add the beef. Shallow fry so it gets a nice crust, then stir. When it is about 90% cooked, strain it.
To the wok, add ginger and garlic (add dried chili if you want it spicy; do not burn the garlic), then add the onions and cook quickly so they do not keep a raw bite.
Add the beef, then the sauce, and lastly all the green onions. Toss together and serve with rice.
notes: Source: Facebook save, Stephvnietea. No recipe text in the caption; transcript names ingredients and steps but gives no quantities, so all quantities are unknown.

title: Crispy Pan-Fried Pork & Shrimp Dumplings
subtitle: Pan-fried dumplings with pork, shiitake and a whole shrimp on each, steamed then crisped
steps: Make the filling: In a large bowl combine ground pork, chopped shiitake mushrooms, chopped green onions, egg, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, chicken stock and salt. Mix well until sticky and fully combined.
Fill the dumplings: Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each dumpling wrapper.
Add the shrimp: Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium heat with a little oil. Place one small shrimp on top of each dumpling, gently pressing it into the filling.

Pan-fry and steam: Cook 1-2 minutes until bottoms begin to brown. Pour in 1/4 cup water, cover and steam 6-7 minutes. Remove lid and cook 1-2 more minutes until water evaporates and bottoms are crispy.
Serve garnished with sliced green onion, chili oil and chili crisp, immediately while hot and crispy.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Series 'EASY MEALS FOR 2, EP 11'; makes about 30 dumplings. Dumpling wrappers are used in the method but not quantified in the ingredient list.

title: Crispy Shrimp, Pork & Chinese Leek Dumplings
subtitle: Pan-fried dumplings with shrimp, pork and Chinese leek, served with soy and chili oil dip

items.name: green onions, finely sliced (2 for filling, 2 for garnish)

steps: Make the filling: Combine ground pork, chopped shrimp, Chinese leek and green onions. Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, chicken bouillon dissolved in the 1/4 cup water, salt, pepper, sesame oil and grated ginger. Mix thoroughly until sticky and well combined.
Fill the dumplings: Spray pan with oil, place spoonfuls of filling on the pan, dip each dumpling wrapper in water and place wrapper over filling. Repeat until all filling is used.

Pan-fry: Cover pan with a lid, turn heat to medium-high until sizzling, then immediately reduce to medium and cook 3-4 minutes. Turn heat back to medium-high, remove lid and cook another 2 minutes until all liquid has evaporated.
Serve garnished with sliced green onions and sesame seeds (optional), alongside the soy sauce and chili oil dipping sauce.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Series 'EASY MEALS FOR 2, EP 16'; makes 21-28 dumplings. Wrappers are easier to work with after lightly dipping in water; start on high only until sizzling, then lower to medium to prevent burning.

title: Mongolian Beef
subtitle: Thin-sliced flank steak seared on a Blackstone or wok with onion and green onion in a savory sauce

items.name: beef flank, thinly sliced into 2-inch strips
green onion stalks, cut into 2-3 inch pieces
dried chilies, optional (4-7, for extra heat)
Shaoxing wine (or dry sherry or dry white wine)
½ tsp white or black pepper

steps: Combine cornstarch, baking soda, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce and white pepper. Add sliced beef and mix well to coat. Marinate 15 minutes.
In a small bowl whisk together oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, soy sauce, sugar, chicken bouillon, sesame oil and pepper. Set aside.

Heat Blackstone griddle (or wok/skillet) to medium-high with enough oil to coat. Spread beef in a single layer and sear about 2 minutes per side until golden and crispy, to about 80% doneness, then move to the side to rest.
Add a bit more oil and saute minced garlic, ginger and dried chilies (if using) until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and stir-fry briefly, keeping it slightly crunchy. Return beef to center, pour in sauce and add green onions. Mix until evenly coated.
Remove from heat and serve hot with steamed rice.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Cooked on a Blackstone in the source; wok or skillet works per the instructions.

title: One-Skillet Cheesy Beef and Pasta Dinner
subtitle: Ground beef and penne simmered in beef broth, finished in a creamy three-cheese sauce
steps: Heat oil and 1 tbsp butter in a skillet. Cook ground beef until browned and slightly crispy. Season with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika and Italian seasoning.
Push beef aside. Add remaining butter, onion and garlic. Cook until soft and fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil. Stir in pasta, cover and simmer until tender.
Reduce heat and stir in heavy cream until combined.
Whisk in cream cheese until smooth.
Add cheddar, Parmesan and mozzarella. Stir until melted and creamy.
Let cheese melt fully, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Prep 10 minutes, cook 30 minutes, about 600 kcal per serving per source. Source tips suggest adding spinach or broccoli, using rotini or shells instead of penne, or red pepper flakes for heat. Salt and black pepper for the beef are listed without quantities in the source.

title: Conchitas con Carne
subtitle: One-pot shell pasta and ground sirloin in a spiced tomato-based sauce
steps: In a Dutch oven or large pot, cook ground sirloin over medium heat until browned. Drain excess fat and return beef to pot.
Add uncooked shell pasta and stir with the beef. Toast 1-2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly golden and fragrant.
Add chopped onion and sliced bell pepper. Sprinkle in cumin, chili powder, paprika, cayenne (if using), garlic powder, salt and black pepper. Stir well to coat.
Mix in tomato sauce until fully incorporated. Crumble in the beef bouillon cube.
Pour in 4-5 cups water, making sure pasta is fully submerged. Bring to a gentle boil and simmer uncovered 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer about 10 minutes, until pasta is tender and sauce has thickened. Stir before serving and enjoy hot.
notes: Source: Facebook save. No servings stated in source, so base servings set to 2. Water is 4-5 cups in source; 4 cups listed.

title: Loaded Taco Lasagna
subtitle: Layered casserole of taco-seasoned beef, tortillas, enchilada sauce and cheese
steps: Season and cook the ground beef with taco seasoning (per the dish description).
Layer seasoned taco beef, flour tortillas, enchilada sauce, refried beans and cheeses in a baking dish, as shown in the video.
Bake as a casserole until the cheese is melted and gooey (time and temperature not stated in the source).
Top with sour cream, tomatoes and green onions and serve.
notes: Source: Facebook save, Mexican Family Recipes. Partial: quantities are from on-screen text in the video; ground beef quantity, bake time and temperature were not in the provided text.

subtitle: Poached shrimp with red onion, jalapeno, avocado, cilantro and citrus

items.name: salt (plenty, should taste like sea water)

steps: Serve with tortilla chips or on a tostada with some smashed avocado.

title: Beef and Broccoli (Herman at Home)
subtitle: Tender beef and blanched broccoli tossed in a savory sauce, served over rice
steps: Season the beef with baking soda, which helps retain moisture, and cornstarch, which coats the meat and makes it velvety.
Blanch the broccoli quickly so it stays crisp and bright green.
Pan fry the beef and set aside.
Saute garlic and ginger, add the sauce, then toss the beef and broccoli in at the end.
Serve over rice.
notes: Source: Facebook save, Herman at Home. Partial: steps are condensed from the video transcript; no quantities were given in the caption or transcript, and the sauce ingredients were not specified. Full recipe was behind a 'comment recipe' link in the source.

title: Crispy Hot Honey Chicken Alfredo
subtitle: Panko-crusted air-fried chicken thighs in hot honey over protein fettuccine with a Greek yogurt Alfredo sauce
steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper, Italian seasoning and garlic powder.
Dredge in flour, dip in egg, then coat in a mixture of panko, parmesan, parsley, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Air fry at 400F for 14-16 minutes, flipping halfway.
Add honey and hot sauce to a pan over medium heat. Simmer until slightly thickened, then toss the chicken in the sauce.
Cook pasta according to package instructions. Reserve 3/4 cup pasta water before draining.
Blend Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, parmesan, garlic, chicken bouillon and skim milk until smooth.
Melt butter in a skillet over low heat. Remove from heat and stir in the blended sauce.
Slowly whisk in pasta water until creamy. Do not let the sauce boil or simmer after adding the yogurt mixture or it may curdle.
Toss with pasta and serve with the hot honey chicken.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Makes 4 servings per source (696 calories, 60g protein per serving). Author notes the sauce curdled in the video and warns not to boil it after adding the yogurt mixture.

title: Dumpling Lasagna
subtitle: Layered wonton wrappers and pork filling steamed in a baking dish
steps: In a large bowl mix all the ingredients for the meat filling.
Grease a baking dish with sesame oil, dip wonton wrappers in water and layer the bottom of the dish. Spread a thin layer of meat filling and repeat the process.
Place the baking dish into a large pan or pot and add water. Pour 1/4 water into the baking dish. Cover with a lid and steam for 45 minutes.
Garnish with green onions and season with soy sauce and chili oil.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Soy sauce and chili oil for finishing are mentioned in the method without quantities. No servings stated in source, so base servings set to 2.

title: Sweet Chili Chicken
subtitle: Air-fried chicken thighs in a sweet chili, soy and oyster sauce marinade, served over rice
steps: Combine the chicken thighs with soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil and chili sauce and marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Lightly spray the air fryer basket with oil. Place the marinated chicken thighs in the basket in a single layer.
Cook at 350F (175C) for about 12 minutes until cooked through and the exterior looks slightly caramelized.
Slice the chicken into thin pieces.
Serve over a bowl of rice. Optionally garnish with sesame seeds and serve with fresh cucumbers.
notes: Source: Facebook save, iamneverfull. Full recipe fetched from the linked recipe page https://iamneverfull.com/sweet-chili-chicken/ because the Facebook caption did not include it. That page lists nutrition as 1 serving.

title: Lemongrass Beef
subtitle: Thin-sliced strip steak marinated with lemongrass and garlic, caramelized in a pan and served over rice
steps: Place the thinly sliced beef in a bowl and marinate with dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, chopped lemongrass and minced garlic for at least 15 minutes, ideally an hour.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat with a bit of oil. Add the beef in a single layer and cook for about 5 minutes, allowing the edges to caramelize.
Stir briefly to finish cooking, making sure the beef is evenly browned and coated in the marinade.
Serve over a fresh bowl of rice and optionally serve with vegetables and crispy onions.
notes: Source: Facebook save, iamneverfull. Full recipe fetched from the linked recipe page https://iamneverfull.com/lemongrass-beef-recipe/ because the Facebook caption did not include it. That page lists nutrition as 1 serving; peanuts were shown as a topping in the Facebook video summary but are not in the linked recipe's ingredient list.

title: Sticky Sweet Chicken
subtitle: Chicken thighs cooked in their soy, honey and brown sugar marinade until it reduces to a sticky glaze, served over rice

items.name: chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized chunks

steps: Place the cubed chicken thighs in a bowl and combine with dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, garlic, brown sugar, honey, rice vinegar and sesame oil. Mix thoroughly and marinate for 15 minutes.

Heat a pan over medium heat with a bit of oil. Add the chicken along with the marinade and cook, stirring occasionally, until fully cooked and the sauce has reduced into a sticky glaze that clings to the chicken.
Remove from the heat and serve over a fresh bowl of rice.
Optionally garnish with scallions.
notes: Source: Facebook save, iamneverfull. Recipe fetched from the linked page https://iamneverfull.com/sticky-sweet-chicken-recipe/ because the Facebook caption did not include quantities; that page lists the chicken amount but does not give quantities for the marinade ingredients, so this extraction is partial. That page lists nutrition as 1 serving.

title: Korean Beef Bulgogi
subtitle: Marinated beef cooked in a skillet and served over rice, from the 'Better Than Takeout' Ep. 9 video
steps: Combine the beef with soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil and gochujang, then grate in the garlic, ginger and half a pear and mix together.
Transfer everything to a plastic bag and marinate overnight.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan, add the beef without overcrowding, and flip after about 2 minutes.
Serve over rice (video shows green onions sprinkled on top).
notes: Source: Facebook save, Zachs.foods. Partial: quantities are not stated in the video transcript and the caption says the full recipe is in the creator's bio, which was not available. Transcript says cooking takes about 20 minutes after the overnight marinade.

title: Poolish Pizza Dough
subtitle: Neapolitan-style pizza dough made with an overnight poolish, demonstrated by pizza master Vito

items.name: olive oil, for the counter and hands

steps: Make the poolish: mix 300g water, 5g yeast and 5g honey, then add 300g flour and mix until it forms one dough.
Cover the poolish (with a few holes so it can breathe) and rest 1 hour at room temperature, then 16 to 24 hours in the fridge.

Make the dough: put all the poolish in the mixer. Reserve a cup of cold water from the 700g to add later, add the remaining water and mix on speed 1 until the water turns white (about 30 seconds to 1 minute).
Add all 1100g flour, then add the 30g salt. Mix for no more than 20 minutes total.
Once the dough has absorbed the flour and the bottom of the bowl is dry, increase speed to about 4-5 and add the reserved cold water little by little, on top of the dough.
Oil the counter. Cut the dough out of the bowl rather than pulling it, then do stretch folds to build the gluten structure, form a large ball, oil the top, and rest 15 minutes.
Cut dough balls of approximately 280g, keeping the top side always on top, close each like a balloon and place upside down in a box, about four fingers apart.
Rest the balls 1 to 2 hours at room temperature until doubled.
notes: Source: Facebook save, Guga Foods. Partial: the transcript ends after the dough balls have risen; topping and baking instructions are not in the text provided. Dough is stated as 75% hydration.

subtitle: Steak tips with rigatoni in a mozzarella cream sauce; ingredients only in the source post

title: Asian-Style Crispy Garlic Chicken
subtitle: Batter-fried chicken thighs tossed in a soy-hoisin garlic sauce

items.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces

steps: In a large bowl, combine the cornstarch, all-purpose flour, baking powder, salt, black pepper, garlic powder and onion powder. Gradually add the cold water, stirring until you have a smooth batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet or wok over medium-high heat; the oil should be about 2 inches deep.

Dip the chicken pieces into the batter, letting any excess drip off. Carefully add the battered chicken to the hot oil, frying in batches to avoid overcrowding. Fry until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, hoisin sauce, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger and red pepper flakes (if using).
In a large skillet or wok, heat a small amount of oil over medium heat. Add the sauce mixture and cook for 1-2 minutes until it begins to simmer.
Add the crispy chicken to the skillet, tossing to coat evenly with the sauce. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until heated through and well coated.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Source: Facebook save. Prep time 15 minutes, cooking time 20 minutes, 400 kcal per serving as stated in the post.

title: Asian Cucumber Salad
subtitle: Salted Persian cucumbers in a garlic, gochugaru and sesame dressing
steps: Slice the Persian cucumbers and toss with 1 tbsp salt; let sit for 15 minutes.
Rinse, drain and pat the cucumbers dry.
Add the minced garlic, gochugaru, sesame oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame seeds and brown sugar, and toss to combine.
notes: Source: Facebook save, My Healthy Dish.

title: Habanero Peach Pork Belly with Caramelized Bourbon Butter
subtitle: Roasted pork belly brushed with a spicy-sweet peach bourbon butter
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Score the pork belly skin in a crisscross pattern and season with salt and pepper. Place in a roasting pan and roast for 2 hours, until crispy and cooked through.
In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the diced habanero peppers and cook until softened.
Add the diced peaches and cook until softened.
Pour in the bourbon and simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the brown sugar and continue to cook until thickened and caramelized.
Remove the pork belly from the oven and brush with the caramelized bourbon butter. Return to the oven for an additional 10 minutes.

title: Homemade Pizza Dough and Pizza Sauce
subtitle: Yeast pizza dough with a simmered homemade tomato pizza sauce
steps: Proofing the yeast: In a bowl add the sugar, 1/2 cup of warm water and one packet of active dry yeast and stir. This can be done right in the base of a stand mixer or in a separate bowl. Allow the yeast to set for 10 minutes.

Mixing the dough: Mix together the flour, salt and Italian seasoning blend (optional) until combined. Add the flour mixture to the yeast mixture. Add 3 tablespoons of the olive oil and an additional 1/2 cup of warm water on top to the dough mixture.

Start the mixer or food processor with the dough attachment. Mix until the flour combines, about a minute. Turn the speed up to medium high and mix for a full five minutes. The dough should pull away from the bowl and be stretchy when done.

Letting the dough rise: Add a tablespoon of olive oil to a heatproof bowl. Brush the oil in a thin layer all over the inside of the bowl. Transfer the dough to the bowl and cover with a clean kitchen towel. Place in a warm place and allow it to rise for 30 minutes.

Stretching the dough: Add a light handful of flour to a clean surface, your rolling pin, and a sprinkle of flour to the dough. Knead the dough just a few times by gently stretching, folding it in half and digging the heels of your hand into the dough. Then roll and stretch the dough.

To make pizza: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees. Oil the pan or add a handful of cornmeal evenly to the pan. Keep stretching the dough until it is about 12 inches across. Cover with toppings then bake for 10-12 minutes or until golden brown.
Pizza sauce - Tomatoes: Pour the tomatoes into a large bowl and using your hands, kitchen shears, or an immersion blender, break the tomatoes down so they're chunky but not completely liquid.

Pizza sauce - Aromatics: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, heat the olive oil, grated onions, oregano, basil, and red pepper flakes. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently. Add garlic and cook for another 30 seconds to a minute.

Pizza sauce - Simmer: Add the prepared tomatoes along with the sugar and salt. Let the sauce reach a simmer, then lower heat to medium-low and simmer for 30 minutes. Taste and adjust seasonings. Sauce can be refrigerated for up to 1 week or frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Jim Lahey's No-Knead Bread
subtitle: The famous 2006 New York Times recipe from Jim Lahey of Sullivan Street Bakery: a shaggy, no-knead dough with a long slow rise, baked in a screaming-hot Dutch oven for a crackling crust and open, chewy crumb. Makes one 1 1/2-pound loaf.

items.name: all-purpose or bread flour, plus more for dusting
cornmeal or wheat bran, as needed for dusting

steps: In a large bowl, combine the flour, yeast, and salt. Add the water and stir until blended; the dough will be shaggy and sticky. Cover with plastic wrap and let rest at least 12 hours, preferably about 18, at warm room temperature (about 70°F).

The dough is ready when its surface is dotted with bubbles. Turn it onto a lightly floured surface, sprinkle with a little more flour, and fold it over on itself once or twice. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and rest 15 minutes.

Using just enough flour to keep the dough from sticking, gently shape it into a ball. Generously coat a cotton towel (not terry cloth) with flour, wheat bran, or cornmeal; place the dough seam-side down on the towel and dust the top with more. Cover with another towel and let rise about 2 hours, until more than doubled and it doesn't spring back when poked.

At least 30 minutes before the dough is ready, heat the oven to 450°F and put a 6- to 8-quart heavy covered pot (Dutch oven) inside to heat. When the dough is ready, carefully remove the hot pot, turn the dough into it seam-side up (it will look messy — that's fine), and shake the pot once or twice to distribute it.
Cover and bake 30 minutes. Remove the lid and bake another 15-30 minutes, until the loaf is deeply browned. Cool on a rack before slicing.
notes: Curated 2026-10-21: your save (Dexter Hughes' video) pointed to this recipe but had no written version. Text is the original Jim Lahey recipe as published by the New York Times (via Mark Bittman), verified word-for-word across multiple reproductions. Hands-on time is only about 30 minutes, but the dough needs 14-20 hours of rising, so start it the day before. Base servings = 1 loaf.
